text:
sophia: FYI ap-southeast1 node-pending tiny jobs surged to ~140 at 04:10 UTC, many failing with FailedScheduling/InsufficientGPU even though node GPUs show free slices. Suspect packing/fragmentation.
liam: any recent autoscaler or descheduler changes rolled?
sophia: autoscaler scale-down config tuned yesterday to be aggressive; also a perf team change added a taint 'redwood/fastpath=true:NoSchedule' to a subset of nodes for latency-sensitive jobs.
raj: that taint sounds relevant. Do the tiny jobs tolerate it?
sophia: no, they don't. Sample describe: 
```
Name:         train-small-cc3f
Status:       Pending
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m (x8 over 12m)  default-scheduler  0/12 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 6 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
```
liam: interesting: InsufficientGPU + taint both. Could be that autoscaler freed full-GPU nodes leaving many fragmented nodes with tiny slices but scheduler prefers nodes with matching topology label gpu.pool=fastpath which are tainted.
raj: do we have node labels changed? run: kubectl get nodes -L gpu.pool,gpu.slab
sophia: returned mix: some nodes labeled gpu.pool=fastpath (tainted), others gpu.pool=shared. The aggressive scale-down removed many shared nodes last night, leaving many fractional allocations on leftover nodes -> fragmentation.
ci-bot: [CI] triggered 48 new tiny jobs at 04:07 UTC (parallel matrix).
liam: CI burst + scale-down + tainted fastpath subset = perfect storm.
sophia: quick mitigation options: 1) add toleration for fastpath on mini jobs (mass patch), 2) adjust autoscaler to keep N extra shared nodes, 3) run descheduler to coalesce fractional pods onto fewer nodes then cordon tainted nodes for eviction, 4) temporarily remove taint on a canary set of nodes.
raj: prefer ephemeral toleration + temporary autoscaler bump. Don't want to remove taint since perf team relies on it.
liam: I'll open a knob: set cluster-autoscaler --scale-down-unneeded-time to 15m to slow down scale-down for 1h, and increase min-shared-nodes to 3.
sophia: I'll mass-patch pending pods with: 
```
kubectl get pods -nml -o name | grep train-small | xargs -n1 kubectl patch --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/tolerations/-","value":{"key":"redwood/fastpath","operator":"Equal","value":"true","effect":"NoSchedule"}}]'
```
(10s later)
sophia: patched ~85 pending pods, observed ~60 transition to Scheduling then Running.
liam: great. raj, can you run a descheduler job to compact fractional GPU pods to fewer nodes? Use policy: low-utilization and remove-duplicates.
raj: running descheduler job now. Also snapshot scheduler logs for postmortem.
sophia: scheduler log snippet: 
```
I0407 04:12:58.456 scheduler: predicate failed: InsufficientGPU for pod train-small-cc3f
I0407 04:13:01.789 scheduler: predicate failed: TaintToleration for pod train-mini-9a2b
```
liam: ops-bot create incident ticket. ops-bot: "Incident #INC-9901 created: ap-southeast1 fragmentation during aggressive scale-down + CI burst"
sre-bot: Alert[FRAG-APSE1]: tiny-pod pending > 100 for 9m.
raj: descheduler finished, reclaimed 12 nodes worth of capacity by consolidating. Starting cordon/evict on 2 underutilized nodes to re-balance.
sophia: action items: liam -> revert aggressive scale-down flags for 1h and add min-shared-nodes; raj -> run descheduler + evict plan; sophia -> mass-patch running job templates to include toleration or update CI matrix to target shared pool; liam -> coordinate perf team to review taint usage and create a stable pool.
liam: cost note: bumping autoscaler min nodes will increase idle cost ~0.6 GPU-hours/hr but avoids retry churn from CI which is higher.
sophia: agree. we'll remove tolerations and restore autoscaler defaults after 24h and follow with a small canary test.
ops-bot: Incident updated: mitigation applied, monitoring for 30m.
sophia: will write a short postmortem with root cause: (CI burst + aggressive scale-down left fractional allocations) + (fastpath taint reduced available nodes) and recommendations: autoscaler safety buffer for fractional workloads, descheduler scheduled after scale-down, and CI rate-limits to smooth bursts.
raj: thanks, will add an infra-runbook checklist for taint rollouts and autoscaler changes. :thumbsup:
